name: Biometric availability and enrollment change
plain: Reads if biometrics are enrolled; iOS also exposes a token that changes when enrollment changes.
meaning: Reveals device security setup. The iOS domain state changes when a new finger or face is added, so it is a weak device-state fingerprint.

android.note: Result codes: SUCCESS, NONE_ENROLLED, NO_HARDWARE, HW_UNAVAILABLE

ios.api_surface: evaluatedPolicyDomainState changes when enrollment changes; Face ID needs usage string only when authenticating

limits.headline: Can check whether you set up fingerprint or face unlock, but not who you are
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the app decides whether to offer biometric sign in
can: Check if the phone has fingerprint or face unlock hardware
Check if you have enrolled at least one fingerprint or face
On iPhone, notice that your enrolled fingerprints or faces changed since last time
Decide whether to show a biometric sign in button
cannot: See your fingerprint, face scan, or any biometric data
Tell which finger or face is enrolled, or how many
Unlock anything without the system scan prompt
limits.differs: iPhone also gives a change marker when someone adds a new finger or face. Android gives only a status such as none enrolled or no hardware.

story.what_it_is: An app can quietly check whether you have set up a fingerprint or face unlock.

marketing.name: BiometricManager
marketing.pitch: Android tells apps whether strong biometric sign in is ready on the device before offering it.

story.for_you: You never see this check. You just notice that an app offers 'Use Face ID' or 'Use fingerprint' only when you have set one up. If you add a new face or finger, some apps may quietly ask you to log in again.
story.for_makers: Makers need to know whether to show the biometric button or fall back to a password. Banks also watch for the enrollment change on iPhone, because a new face added right before a big transfer can mean someone else has the phone.

use_cases.example: A bank app checks that you have fingerprint unlock set up, then offers a one tap login instead of a long password.
A bank notices a new face was added to a phone an hour ago and asks for a full password and a code before it allows a large transfer.
A password manager shows an 'Unlock with Face ID' toggle only when the phone can actually do it.
A payments app skips the biometric prompt on a phone with no enrolled finger and asks for a PIN instead.
A work app checks that biometrics are set up so company data is protected by more than a 4 digit code.
An ad or fraud tool adds the enrollment state to a quiet device profile, which helps tell one phone from another.

story.android_note: Android only says whether strong biometrics are ready (yes, none enrolled, no hardware). It does not give a change token.
story.ios_note: iPhone apps can read a token that changes whenever someone adds or removes a face or finger, which acts as a small device state signal.
